title: Integer to English Words
statement:
Spell out the non-negative integer `num` in English and return the result as a string. Follow these rules exactly:

- Words are separated by single spaces, each starts with a capital letter, and there are no hyphens, commas, the word "And", or extra spaces at either end.
- `0` is written `"Zero"`; zero is never spelled anywhere else.
- Split `num` into groups of three digits from the right. Write each nonzero group, followed by its scale word `Billion`, `Million` or `Thousand` (none for the lowest group), from the highest group down, and leave out groups that are `000` entirely.
- A group is written as: its hundreds digit's name followed by `Hundred` when that digit is nonzero; then the rest (`1` to `99`): `One` through `Nineteen` for values below 20, otherwise the tens word (`Twenty`, `Thirty`, `Forty`, `Fifty`, `Sixty`, `Seventy`, `Eighty`, `Ninety`) followed by the units digit's name when that digit is not zero.

examples.name: Example 2
examples.expected: Twelve Thousand Three Hundred Forty Five

examples.name: Example 3
examples.expected: One Million Two Hundred Thirty Four Thousand Five Hundred Sixty Seven

notes:
## Intuition

English names large numbers three digits at a time: 1,234,567 is "one million", then "two hundred thirty four thousand", then "five hundred sixty seven". Every group is spelled the same way whatever its position; only the scale word after it (`Billion`, `Million`, `Thousand` or nothing) changes. So the whole problem reduces to spelling a number below 1000 and gluing the groups together, skipping groups that are zero.

## Approach

1. Return `"Zero"` straight away for `0`; it is the only case where zero is spelled.
2. Keep lookup tables: `ones` for 1 to 19, `tens` for the multiples of ten from 20, and `scales` for the group names.
3. `chunkWords(chunk)` spells a value from 1 to 999: the hundreds digit plus `Hundred` if present, then the tens word if the rest is 20 or more, then any remaining 1 to 19 from `ones`.
4. Walk `scale` from 3 (billions) down to 0, cutting out each three-digit `chunk` with division and `% 1000`.
5. Skip chunks equal to 0; otherwise append the chunk's words and, above the lowest group, its scale word.
6. Join `words` with single spaces.

## Example 1, step by step

`num = 123`. The chunks for billions, millions and thousands are all 0 and are skipped. At `scale = 0`, `chunk = 123`: `chunkWords` adds `One Hundred` and leaves 23, adds `Twenty` and leaves 3, then adds `Three`. No scale word is added, so the answer is `"One Hundred Twenty Three"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): at most four groups of a few words each.
- Space: O(1): fixed tables and a short word list.

## Pitfalls

- A zero group in the middle (1,000,010) must add nothing, not `Thousand` on its own.
- Values 10 to 19 have their own names: 13 is `Thirteen`, never `Ten Three`.
- Round tens such as 40 must not get a trailing `Zero`, and the word is spelled `Forty`.
- Joining pieces with spaces as you go easily leaves double or trailing spaces; collecting words and joining once avoids that.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ones` | names of 1 to 19 (index 0 unused) |
| `tens` | names of 20, 30, ..., 90 by tens digit |
| `scales` | scale word for each group, from units up to billions |
| `chunk` | the three-digit group being spelled |
| `parts` | words of one group |
| `words` | words of the whole answer |
| `scale` | which group is being read (3 = billions, 0 = units) |

narration.2: Zero is the one number that is spelled with the word Zero.
narration.3: Return it at once; every other answer leaves zero groups out.
narration.5: Names of 1 to 19; index 0 is empty because a zero part adds no word.
narration.6: Names of the multiples of ten from twenty, indexed by the tens digit.
narration.7: Scale word for each group of three digits, from the lowest group up.
narration.9: chunkWords spells one group, a value from 1 to 999.
narration.12: Name the hundreds digit and add the word Hundred.
narration.13: Keep only the last two digits.
narration.15: Twenty or more uses a tens word.
narration.16: Add the tens word, such as Forty.
narration.19: Whatever is left (1 to 19) has its own name.
narration.22: Return the words of this group.
narration.26: Read the groups from billions (scale 3) down to units (scale 0).
narration.27: Cut out this group's three digits.
narration.28: An all-zero group says nothing at all.
narration.31: Add the words for this group.
narration.32: Every group above the units has a scale word.
narration.36: Join all the words with single spaces.
